extracted.intended_audience: applicants and representatives filing European patent applications (patent attorneys, agents, applicants)
extracted.subtask_description: Requirements and procedural/formal rules for preparing, filing, and prosecuting European patent applications under the Implementing Regulations to the European Patent Convention. Covers content, format, fees, search and publication procedures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rule 24 — Filing procedure and receipt obligations
rubrics_metrics.description: European patent applications may be filed directly or by post. The authority with which the application is filed shall mark the documents with the date of receipt and issue without delay a receipt including at least the application number, the nature and number of the documents and the date of their receipt. If filed with an authority referred to in Article 75(1)(b) it shall inform the European Patent Office without delay of receipt, nature and date of receipt, the application number and any priority date claimed. When the EPO receives an application forwarded by a central industrial property office it shall inform the applicant of the EPO date of receipt.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Procedural obligations on receiving offices to date-stamp, issue receipts with minimum content, and communicate forwarded filings and priority information to the EPO; EPO to notify applicants when national offices forward applications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rule 25 — Divisional applications: timing, content and fees
rubrics_metrics.description: A European divisional application may be filed at any time after receipt of the earlier European application provided it is filed within any period prescribed after the first communication from the Examining Division or is otherwise considered justified; or within two months following a limitation at invitation of the Examining Division if the earlier application failed Article 82. Description and drawings should, where possible, relate only to the matter for which protection is sought; if necessary they may include a cross-reference to another application. Filing, search and designation fees must be paid for each divisional within one month after filing. Designation fees may be paid up to the expiry of the period specified for the earlier application if that later expiry follows the one-month period.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Timing constraints for filing divisionals, expectation that divisional documents stay focused on claimed subject-matter (or cross-reference when overlap needed), and strict short deadlines for fees (one month) with limited deferral for designation fees tied to Article 79(2) periods.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rule 26 — Contents of the request for grant
rubrics_metrics.description: The request for grant must be filed on an EPO form and shall contain: (a) a petition for grant; (b) the title of the invention clearly and concisely stating the technical designation and excluding fancy names (if multiple claim categories this must be evident from the title); (c) name, address and nationality of applicant with format rules for natural and legal persons and adequate postal address (recommend telegraphic/telephone details); (d) representative's name and business address if appointed; (e) indication if application is a divisional and number of earlier application; (f) number of original European application where Article 61(1)(b) applies; (g) declaration claiming priority with date and country; (h) designation of Contracting State(s) for protection; (i) signature of applicant or representative; (j) list of accompanying documents indicating number of sheets of description, claims, drawings and abstract filed; (k) designation of inventor where applicant is inventor. If multiple applicants, request should preferably appoint one common representative.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the official EPO form; include all required identification, priority and procedural data and the list of submitted parts; adhere to naming/address formatting conventions; appoint a common representative if multiple applicants to simplify correspondence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rule 27 — Description: required content and order
rubrics_metrics.description: The description shall: (a) state the title as in the request; (b) specify the technical field; (c) indicate background art useful for understanding the invention and preferably cite documents; (d) disclose the invention, as claimed, so that the technical problem and its solution can be understood and state advantageous effects with reference to background art; (e) briefly describe figures in drawings; (f) describe in detail at least one embodiment of the claimed invention using examples where appropriate and referring to drawings; (g) explicitly indicate industrial applicability where not obvious. The description shall be presented in the manner and order specified unless another order better serves understanding and economy of presentation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Description must enable understanding of problem-solution and at least one practicable embodiment; include background and advantages; follow prescribed structure unless deviating improves clarity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rule 28 — Micro-organism-related disclosure and deposit requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: For inventions involving a non-public micro-organism, the application and resulting patent are only regarded as sufficiently disclosed if: (a) a culture was deposited in a recognized collection not later than the filing date; (b) the application gives available relevant information on characteristics of the micro-organism; (c) the culture collection, deposit date and deposit file number are given. The information in (c) may be submitted within two months after filing. Deposits shall be available to any person from publication date subject to undertakings (e.g., not to make available to others; pre-grant use only for experimental purposes if requested before grant). Undertakings cease if application refused/withdrawn or on expiry of patent. Compulsory licences may permit use without the undertaking. The EPO President will publish recognised collections and conclude agreements regarding deposit, storage and availability.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Strict deposit and disclosure regime for biological materials: timely deposit, identification in the application (or within two months), public availability rules and confidentiality/usage undertakings pre-grant; EPO maintains list of accepted culture collections.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rule 29 — Form and content of claims
rubrics_metrics.description: Claims shall define the subject-matter sought in terms of technical features. Where appropriate, claims shall contain: (a) a statement indicating designation of the subject-matter and technical features necessary for definition but which are part of the prior art; (b) a characterising portion preceded by 'characterised in that' or 'characterised by' stating the technical features which in combination with (a) are desired to be protected. Subject to Article 82, multiple independent claims in the same category are permitted if appropriate. Claims stating essential features may be followed by claims to particular embodiments. Dependent claims including all features of another claim shall, if possible at the beginning, reference that claim and then state additional features. Dependent claims may refer to dependent claims. Dependent claims referring back to single or multiple previous claims should be grouped appropriately. Number of claims must be reasonable; claims numbered consecutively in Arabic numerals. Claims should not, except where absolutely necessary, rely on references to description or drawings (e.g., 'as described in part...'). Where drawings exist, reference signs may be used in claims (in parentheses) to increase intelligibility but are not limiting.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Draft claims in clear technical-feature language, use characterising clause format for distinguishing features, keep claim count reasonable, number consecutively, avoid reliance on description/drawings for essential features; dependent claims must reference and add features correctly; reference signs may be used but are non-limiting.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rule 30 — Claims in different categories (combinations permitted)
rubrics_metrics.description: Article 82 permits that the same application may include, e.g., in addition to an independent product claim an independent claim for a process specially adapted for manufacturing the product and an independent claim for a use of the product; or in addition to a process claim an independent claim for an apparatus or means specifically designed for carrying out the process; or combinations of product/process/apparatus claims as appropriate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Permitted to claim related aspects (product, process, apparatus, use) in the same application where appropriate to cover the subject-matter comprehensively.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rule 31 — Claims fees and consequences
rubrics_metrics.description: Any application comprising more than ten claims at filing shall incur a claims fee for each claim over ten, payable within one month after filing. The rule applies mutatis mutandis where the application comprises more claims incurring fees at the date of communication of the Examining Division than at filing, or where it comprises more than ten claims at that date only; such claims fee is payable within the period laid down in that provision. If a claims fee is not paid in due time the claim concerned shall be deemed abandoned. No claims fee duly paid shall be refunded.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Monitor claim count and timely pay claims fees to avoid abandonment; additional claims arising later can trigger fees with corresponding deadlines; fees are non-refundable once paid.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rule 32 — Drawings: format and execution requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Sheets containing drawings: usable surface shall not exceed 26.2 cm x 17 cm; no frames round usable surface. Minimum margins specified (top 2.5 cm, left 2.5 cm, right 1.5 cm, bottom 1 cm). Drawings executed in durable black or blue uniformly thick well-defined lines without colourings. Cross-sections indicated by hatching that should not impede reading of reference signs and lines. Scale and execution such that photographic reproduction with linear reduction to two-thirds still distinguishes all details; if scale given, represent graphically. Numbers, letters and reference signs must be simple and clear; avoid brackets, circles or inverted commas with numbers/letters. Lines ordinarily drawn with drafting instruments. Elements of same figure in proportion unless difference needed for clarity. Height of numbers/letters not less than 0.32 cm; use Latin (and where customary Greek) alphabets. Same sheet may contain several figures; multi-sheet figures arranged so whole can be assembled without concealing parts; figures arranged without wasting space preferably upright and clearly separated; figures numbered consecutively in Arabic numerals independently of sheet numbering. Reference signs not mentioned in description/claims shall not appear in drawings and vice versa; same features must use same reference signs throughout. Drawings should not contain text matter except when absolutely indispensable a single word or words (e.g., 'water', 'steam', 'open', 'closed', 'section on AB') and catchwords for circuits/flow diagrams; such words must be replaceable by translations. Flow sheets and diagrams are considered drawings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Strict physical and graphical standards to ensure reproducibility and legibility after reduction; limit textual labels; maintain consistent reference signs; follow margin and size rules; use drafting instruments and minimum lettering sizes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rule 33 — Abstract: content, length and purpose
rubrics_metrics.description: Abstract must indicate the title of the invention and contain a concise summary of disclosure as in description, claims and drawings; indicate technical field, allow clear understanding of technical problem, gist of solution and principal use(s). Where applicable include the chemical formula that best characterises the invention. Abstract must not contain statements on alleged merits or speculative application. Preferably not more than 150 words. If drawings exist applicant should indicate figures suggested to accompany the abstract; EPO may publish other figures if considered better. Each main feature in abstract illustrated by a drawing should be followed by a reference sign in parentheses. The abstract shall be drafted to constitute an efficient instrument for searching in the technical field and to help decide whether to consult the full application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Keep abstract concise (<=150 words preferred), factual and focused on problem/solution/uses; avoid promotional language; indicate suggested figure(s) and include reference signs for illustrated features; write abstract to aid searchers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rule 34 — Prohibited matter and publication omissions
rubrics_metrics.description: European patent applications shall not contain: (a) matter contrary to ordre public or morality; (b) statements disparaging products/processes of any person other than applicant, or merits/validity of others' applications or patents (mere comparisons with prior art not disparaging per se); (c) any statement obviously irrelevant or unnecessary. If prohibited matter under (a) appears, EPO shall omit it on publication and indicate place and number of words/drawings omitted. If statements under (b) appear EPO may omit them on publication, indicate place and number of words omitted, and furnish upon request a copy of the omitted passages.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid immoral, public-order-violating, disparaging or irrelevant content in applications; EPO will redact such matter from published documents and indicate omissions while providing copies on request in some cases.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rule 35 — Presentation and physical characteristics of application documents
rubrics_metrics.description: Translations under Article 14(2) are included as documents making up the application. Documents shall be filed in three copies (except the request and certain Article 14(2) documents). Documents must admit direct reproduction by photography, electrostatic processes, photo-offset and micro-filming; sheets free from cracks, creases and folds; only one side used. Documents on A4 paper (29.7 x 21 cm) pliable, strong, white, smooth, matt and durable; each sheet used with short sides at top/bottom (upright) subject to Rule 32 exceptions. Each document (request, description, claims, drawings and abstract) shall commence on a new sheet; sheets connected so they can be turned over, separated and joined easily. Minimum and recommended maximum margins specified (top of first sheet 8 cm, top of other sheets 2 cm, left 2.5 cm, right 2 cm, bottom 2 cm; recommended maxima also given). Margins when submitted must be completely blank. All sheets shall be numbered in consecutive Arabic numerals at top middle but not in top margin. Lines of description and claims preferably numbered in sets of five on left side. Request, description, claims and abstract shall be typed or printed; only graphical symbols and chemical/mathematical formulae may be handwritten or drawn. Typing shall be 1.5 spaced; all text characters with capital letters not less than 0.21 cm high and in a dark indelible colour. Request, description, claims and abstract shall not contain drawings. Description and abstract may contain tables; claims may contain tables only if subject-matter makes tables desirable. Units expressed in metric system (or also expressed in metric if other units used); temperatures in Celsius (and also given in Celsius if other system used); densities and other physical values use metric/international practice. Terminology and signs shall be consistent throughout. Each sheet should be reasonably free from erasures and free from alterations, overwritings and interlineations unless authorised where authenticity not in question and reproduction not jeopardised.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Comply with detailed physical/formatting, paper, margin and typographical standards to ensure reproducibility; provide three copies; maintain consistent terminology and legibility standards; avoid drawings in textual parts; adhere to metric units and presentation conventions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rule 36 — Documents filed subsequently: format, signatures and copies
rubrics_metrics.description: Rules 27, 29 and 32 to 35 apply to documents replacing application documents. All other post-filing documents shall normally be typewritten or printed and have a left margin of about 2.5 cm. Documents filed after filing (except annexed documents) must be signed; if not signed EPO shall invite signature within a time limit and if signed in time the document retains its original receipt date, otherwise it shall be deemed not received. Documents that must be communicated to other persons or relate to two or more applications/patents must be filed in sufficient copies; missing copies must be provided at the expense of the party if requested by EPO. As exception, documents may be sent by telegram/telex but a reproducing document complying with requirements must be filed within two weeks of receipt of the telegram/telex; otherwise the telegram/telex is deemed not received.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure post-filing documents follow presentation rules, are signed timely to retain receipt date, file sufficient copies for communications, and follow up telegram/telex submissions with proper reproduced documents within two weeks.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rule 37 — Renewal fees: due dates and special rules
rubrics_metrics.description: Renewal fees for the coming year are due on the last day of the month containing the anniversary of the filing date. Renewal fees may not be validly paid more than one year before due. Fees shall be paid at the rate in force on the day they fall due. Any renewal fee due within three months after an increase and paid on or before the due date but only to the amount valid before increase shall be deemed valid provided the deficit is made good within six months of the due date (no additional fee required). Renewal fees for a European divisional application already due must be paid within four months of filing such divisional. Renewal fees shall not be payable for a new European application filed pursuant to Article 61(1)(b) in respect of the year it was filed and any preceding year.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Observe monthly anniversary due dates, limitation on early payments (max one year early), rules for handling fee increases and shortfalls, and special provisions for divisionals and Article 61(1)(b) new applications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rule 38 — Priority declaration and filing of priority documents
rubrics_metrics.description: The declaration of priority must state the date of previous filing, the State in which it was made and indicate the file number. Date and State of previous filing must be stated on filing the European application; file number must be indicated before the end of the 16th month after the date of priority. Copy of the previous application required for claiming priority must be filed before the end of the 16th month after priority date, certified as an exact copy by the authority which received the previous application and accompanied by a certificate stating the date of filing of the previous application. Where translation of the previous application into one of the EPO official languages is required, the translation must be filed within 20 months after the date of priority. The particulars stated in the declaration of priority shall appear in the published European application and on the European patent specification.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Timely file certified copies and required translations of priority documents and ensure priority particulars are complete and entered within strict 16- and 20-month deadlines to preserve priority claims.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rule 39 — Communication after examination on filing (rectification of filing deficiencies)
rubrics_metrics.description: If the application fails to meet Article 80 requirements, the Receiving Section shall communicate disclosed deficiencies to the applicant and inform him that the application will not be dealt with as a European patent application unless he remedies the deficiencies within one month. If remedied, the applicant shall be informed of the filing date.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Respond promptly (within one month) to Receiving Section deficiency communications to secure filing status and obtain filing date confirmation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rule 40 — Physical requirements cross-referenced
rubrics_metrics.description: The physical requirements which the European patent application must satisfy pursuant to Article 91(1)(b) are those prescribed in Rule 32(1) and (2), Rule 35(2) to (11) and (14), and Rule 36(2) and (4).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure compliance with the specified drawing, document presentation, and subsequent-document provisions referenced here to meet Article 91 physical requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rule 41 — Rectification of deficiencies and limits on amendments
rubrics_metrics.description: If examination under Article 91(1)(a)-(d) and (g) reveals deficiencies, the Receiving Section shall inform the applicant and invite remedy within a specified period. The description, claims and drawings may be amended only to an extent sufficient to remedy the disclosed deficiencies in accordance with the Receiving Section's observations. Paragraph 1 does not apply where the applicant omitted to indicate date or State of first filing while claiming priority, nor where the date of first filing given precedes the actual filing date by more than one year (in which event applicant must indicate corrected date within one month or no right of priority).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Amend only as necessary to correct identified defects; priority-date omissions and more-than-one-year discrepancies are treated specially with tight correction deadlines.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rule 42 — Subsequent identification of the inventor
rubrics_metrics.description: If examination reveals the inventor has not been identified per Rule 17, the Receiving Section shall inform the applicant that the application shall be deemed withdrawn unless this deficiency is corrected within the period prescribed by Article 91(5). For divisionals or new applications under Article 61(1)(b), the time limit for identifying the inventor may not expire before two months after the communication which states the time limit.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide inventor identification within the prescribed time or risk deemed withdrawal; special minimum two-month period for divisionals and certain re-filed applications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rule 43 — Handling late-filed or missing drawings and re-dating
rubrics_metrics.description: If drawings were filed later than the filing date, the Receiving Section shall inform the applicant that the drawings and references to them shall be deemed deleted unless the applicant requests within one month re-dating to the date on which drawings were filed. If drawings were not filed, applicant is invited to file them within one month; application will be re-dated to the date they are filed, or references deleted if not filed in time. Applicant shall be informed of any new filing date.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: File drawings by the filing date to avoid deletion of references or re-dating; if late-filed, promptly request re-dating within one month to preserve drawing references.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rule 44 — Content of the European search report
rubrics_metrics.description: The search report shall mention those documents available to the EPO at the time of drawing up the report which may be taken into consideration for novelty and inventive step. Each citation shall be referred to the claims to which it relates and, if necessary, the relevant parts identified (e.g., page/column/lines or diagrams). The report shall distinguish documents published before the date of priority claimed, between priority date and filing date, and on or after filing date. Any document referring to an oral disclosure, use or other non-written disclosure prior to filing shall be mentioned with an indication of date of publication, if any, and date of non-written disclosure. The search report shall be drawn up in the language of the proceedings and shall contain classification according to the international classification.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Search report must map citations to claims, classify by publication timing relative to priority/filing, record non-written disclosures with dates, be in proceedings language and include IPC classification.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rule 45 — Incomplete search procedures
rubrics_metrics.description: If the Search Division considers that a meaningful search cannot be carried out into the state of the art on the basis of all or some claims, it shall either declare that search is not possible or shall, as far as practicable, draw up a partial European search report. Such declaration or partial report shall be considered, for subsequent proceedings, as the European search report.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Expect partial reports or 'search not possible' declarations when claims prevent a meaningful full search; these are treated as the official search report for later steps.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rule 46 — Search report when unity of invention lacking and fee handling
rubrics_metrics.description: If Search Division considers the application lacks unity, it shall draw up the search report on those parts relating to the invention or group of inventions first mentioned in the claims, and inform the applicant that additional search reports for other inventions require payment of necessary search fees within a period fixed by the Search Division (not less than two weeks and not more than six weeks). The Search Division shall draw up search reports for those parts for which fees were paid. Any fee paid under this paragraph shall be refunded if during examination the applicant requests a refund and the Examining Division finds the communication was not justified.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When lack of unity is raised, be prepared to pay further search fees within the provided (2–6 week) window to obtain searches on non-primary inventions; fees can be refunded if later deemed unjustified by Examining Division.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rule 47 — Definitive content of the abstract determined with search report
rubrics_metrics.description: At the same time as drawing up the European search report, the Search Division shall determine the definitive content of the abstract and transmit it to the applicant together with the search report.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Abstract's final wording is set by the Search Division concurrently with the search report and applicants receive that definitive abstract for publication.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rule 48 — Technical preparations for publication
rubrics_metrics.description: The President of the EPO shall determine when technical preparations for publication of the application are completed. The application shall not be published if it has been finally refused, withdrawn or deemed withdrawn before completion of those technical preparations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Publication timing is subject to EPO's technical-preparation completion; final refusal/withdrawal before that point prevents publication.
